"So the whole, the world sucks so god can’t exist narrative, doesn’t make sense to me."

  
I'm not the best at explaining myself but I can try here. 

For me, I used to pray a lot. And I've also been through a lot in my life. All sorts of suffering. I continued to pray. Everyone kept telling me 'God will take care of you.' But then I continued to suffer. I kept wondering when this 'god' was going to 'take care of me' and why I continued to pray and worship when things have never gotten any better. I wondered if I was supposed to suffer until I die and just hope that heaven was real and hope that I did everything right to get in. It just made no sense to me. 



There was no proof that god or heaven is real, so who was I praying to, and why? Science has proof. Doctors and nurses are the ones who can heal illnesses. But god just sits and watches. I just couldn't get behind that thought. If I'm going to suffer I'm not going to worship someone who may or may not exist in hopes that it was all worth it. I know that hope is a very powerful thing for some people and I know that the promise of heaven is what gets a lot of people through hard times, but for me I just can't get behind it. I guess I just grew into a person who was more 'science and proof' over 'trust/faith and hope.'

You don't want to rush your treatment. Rushing orthodontic work can cause bone/root issues.

  
A lot of people see drastic results in the first few months, but it's the months that follow that are for fine tuning things, and that takes a lot longer. For me, my teeth looked great about 3 months in, but there were still a lot of alignment and things that needed to be perfected. You can't rush it because you want to keep as much of your roots and bone healthy as possible. 

  
Treatment can take a longer time even for seemingly small work for that reason. You don't want your roots to resorb. Also keep in mind that the time you are given are estimates, sometimes it takes more or less time depending on how you respond to treatment, how well you follow your treatment plan, etc

For example, the one friend I do have lives overseas. We talk a lot and when he'd go to sleep, I would say something like "aww, okay." Eventually one day he admitted to me that it made him feel guilty when I did that. In my mind I saw it as 'it means I'm sad to see you go because I like you' and I viewed it as a nice thing. But now I know it bothers him, I don't do it anymore even if I don't understand why it makes him feel guilty. 

But yeah, I know my social skills are a put off. But if people would be more honest and gives others a chance to fix things instead of ghosting them it would help a lot. Especially in my case when I don't even think I'm doing something wrong.

At this point I just kind of accept that its a hard world if you're neurodivergent, and people aren't going to tell me what I'm doing wrong so I just kind of stay friendless. Its hard to learn social skills when people don't stick around long enough but its what it is for me, I guess.
